questions.q: What are the two phases every RAG system has?
options: Training and fine-tuning
Ingestion (ahead of time) and query time (when a user asks a question)
Compression and decompression
Login and logout
questions.explain: Ingestion happens on its own schedule before any question is asked; query time happens live, the instant a user submits a question, and needs to be fast.

options: The user's question is embedded and compared to stored vectors
The LLM generates its final answer
Documents are split into chunks, each chunk is embedded, and the vectors are stored in a vector database
The model's weights are permanently updated
questions.explain: Ingestion is the ahead-of-time preparation step: documents become chunks, chunks become vectors, and those vectors are stored for later retrieval.

questions.q: In the query-time loop, what must match between ingestion and query time?
options: The embedding model used to embed the query must be the same one used to embed the documents
The number of documents must be identical
The user must ask the exact same question every time
The LLM used for generation must also have performed the ingestion
questions.explain: Because similarity search only makes sense when vectors come from the same embedding space, the query must be embedded with the same model used to embed the stored documents.

questions.q: What does 'top-k' refer to in the retrieval step?
options: The number of top-ranked chunks a similarity search returns
The number of LLMs used in parallel
The maximum number of documents a vector database can store
The number of users querying the system at once
questions.explain: Top-k is simply how many of the closest-matching chunks the vector database hands back for the LLM to use as context.

questions.q: Why does this course cover embeddings and vector databases (Chapters 2-3) before the full pipeline (Chapter 4)?
options: Because chunking and prompt assembly are not actually part of RAG
Because embeddings and vector databases are the foundation retrieval quality depends on — if retrieval pulls back the wrong chunks, no prompting technique fixes a bad answer
Because the LLM generation step is optional and covered last
Alphabetical ordering of the topics
questions.explain: Poor-quality retrieval caused by a weak embedding model or a misconfigured vector store undermines every later step, so the course builds that foundation first.
